name: Well-differentiated Thymic Neuroendocrine Carcinoma

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of well-differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma of thymic origin with neuroendocrine markers positivity
Radiological evidence of an anterior mediastinal mass consistent with thymic origin
Positive immunohistochemical staining for chromogranin A, synaptophysin, and CD56
Exclusion of metastatic neuroendocrine tumors from other primary sites

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with positive neuroendocrine markers and radiological evidence of thymic origin, excluding metastatic disease
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary correlation including pathology, radiology, and clinical findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Anterior mediastinal mass detected on imaging
pathognomonic.notes: Often asymptomatic initially, detected incidentally or due to mass effect
searchTerms: mass in front of chest detected by scan

pathognomonic.symptomName: Paraneoplastic Cushing syndrome due to ectopic ACTH secretion
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic hormonal syndrome in some cases
searchTerms: excess cortisol due to tumor hormone

common.symptomName: Chest pain localized to anterior mediastinum
common.notes: Due to tumor invasion or compression
searchTerms: chest pain in front of chest

common.notes: From mass effect on lungs or airways

searchTerms: unintentional weight loss and poor appetite

common.notes: Due to vascular compression by tumor

searchTerms: drooping eyelid, small pupil, and lack of sweating
Horner's syndrome signs including ptosis and miosis
eye and facial symptoms from nerve damage

occasional.symptomName: Hoarseness from recurrent laryngeal nerve compression
searchTerms: voice changes due to laryngeal nerve

occasional.notes: Rare ectopic insulin-like growth factor secretion

searchTerms: low energy from ongoing health issues

occasional.notes: Due to tumor invasion or lymphatic obstruction

searchTerms: autoimmune muscle weakness related to cancer

rare.symptomName: Superior mediastinal syndrome with airway obstruction
searchTerms: upper chest pressure causing breathing issues

rare.symptomName: Hypercalcemia due to paraneoplastic secretion of PTHrP
searchTerms: high blood calcium from tumor hormone

laboratory: Elevated serum ACTH and cortisol levels in cases with ectopic Cushing syndrome
Neuroendocrine tumor markers elevated: chromogranin A, neuron-specific enolase
Possible hypoglycemia in rare cases due to ectopic insulin-like factors
imaging: CT or MRI showing anterior mediastinal mass with possible invasion of adjacent structures
Somatostatin receptor scintigraphy or PET scan demonstrating neuroendocrine tumor activity
genetic: No specific germline mutations identified; sporadic cases predominate
Possible MEN1 gene mutations in rare familial cases
other: Histopathology showing organoid nesting, trabecular or rosette patterns with neuroendocrine differentiation
Immunohistochemistry positive for chromogranin A, synaptophysin, CD56

distinguishingFeatures: Clinical history of neuroendocrine tumor elsewhere
Primary lung mass rather than thymic

redFlags: Rapidly progressive superior vena cava syndrome
Severe paraneoplastic Cushing syndrome with electrolyte imbalance
Signs of airway obstruction or respiratory failure
references: Travis WD, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Lung, Pleura, Thymus and Heart. IARC; 2021.
